results.evaluation_method: tau2-bench original tau-bench (None submission by Anthropic)

extra.notes: Scores were achieved with a prompt addendum to both the Airline and Retail Agent Policy instructing Claude to better leverage its reasoning abilities while using extended thinking with tool use. The model is encouraged to write down its thoughts as it solves the problem distinct from our usual thinking mode, during the multi-turn trajectories to best leverage its reasoning abilities. To accommodate the additional steps Claude incurs by utilizing more thinking, the maximum number of steps (counted by model completions) was increased from 30 to 100 (most trajectories completed under 30 steps with only one trajectory reaching above 50 steps).

Cortex 0.1 is a cognitive architecture from Principled Machines. A cognitive core directs the work; a language model is one kind of compute it uses, for semantic judgement, and other parts of a task go to retrieval, programs and other specialized components. We attribute the result to two mechanisms: enhanced retrieval for multi-hop questions over the knowledge base, and process-calculus abstractions for the policy workflows. Submitted as custom because Cortex replaces the standard single-model scaffold. No task-specific fine-tuning, no prompt tuning against the grader, no post-training on labels, and no autoresearch loop. Cost is the average agent spend per trajectory, excluding the user simulator. Write-up: https://principledmachines.com/research/tau3-banking/

Distyl ButtonAgent uses GPT-5.4 with high reasoning effort and a custom agentic retrieval pipeline powered by Mixedbread semantic search (mxbai-wholembed-v3). The 698 banking knowledge documents are indexed in a hosted Mixedbread vector store and retrieved dynamically during conversation. 4 trials. Seed: 300.

Custom voice evaluation on all 97 banking_knowledge base tasks, regular speech, alltools retrieval, one trial. Run seed 300; trial 0 seed 626729. Agent openai_live:gpt-live-1 delegates to gpt-6-astra at high effort, with marin voice and priority service. Caller openai/responses/gpt-5.5 uses xhigh effort and ElevenLabs eleven_v3 with native persona voices; full reviewer openai/gpt-5.5. Native error and hallucination retry limits are three; one 15-worker controller. Sierra tau2-bench 1.0.1, base 2174a603f6d014ef94473ffa95957f6ce27100db, with local execution/resource changes; task definitions, policies, prompts and native grading logic unchanged. The entire high run was selected from two complete ElevenLabs candidates (high and xhigh), with no per-task best-of mixing. Includes all 97 canonical histories, combined both.wav recordings, native label files, and original rewards and reviews. Custom submission: base model is xAI grok-voice-think-fast-1.0 (audio-native, regular speech complexity, single trial on the full base splits) with an added tool-boundary mentor — a separate LLM (gemini-3.5-flash, reasoning_effort=high, read/write deadlines 10s/15s, fail-open) that reviews the voice agent's tool calls at runtime: pre-execution gates on state-mutating and escalation calls (transfer_to_human_agents), guidance notes appended to read results, and stop-interception so a blocked hand-off proposal continues the conversation. The mentor receives only agent-visible inputs (agent-heard STT transcript, official tool results, the same domain policy the agent receives, agent tool names and descriptions); its prompt contains no benchmark-derived facts and is published verbatim in the referenced fork together with its content policy. Standard tau2 agent and user-simulator prompts are byte-unmodified; the mentor is an additional component with its own prompt. Explicit xAI server-VAD settings (threshold 0.1, silence 1200ms, prefix padding 600ms) and 2.0x input gain restore a working audio pipeline on the July 2026 xAI serving stack (in our environment, server-default VAD frequently failed to detect user speech, and we were unable to reproduce the April 2026 official score with default settings). All non-mentor behavioral differences from upstream are enumerated in the referenced methodology document; submitted runs used the upstream-compatible voice-seed behavior (TAU2_OFFICIAL_PYTHON_HASH_VOICE_SEED=1). The voice user-simulator pipeline is the standard v1.0 lineage with only its LLM swapped: gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 at reasoning_effort=xhigh — not comparable to standard-user-simulator leaderboard entries. Voices are local ElevenLabs personas, not Sierra-managed submission voices.

Standard submission from Pine AI. The agent is a two-agent system: (1) a voice agent handling real-time speech via a customized ASR -> LLM -> TTS pipeline coordinated by a custom interaction model that governs turn-taking, backchanneling, and other conversational dynamics; (2) a background agent (gemini-4-argon, reasoning_effort=high) that issues the tool calls for the operational task. The two agents share context.
All voice-side models are the same production models serving 19pine.ai -- not benchmark-trained. No files in this tau-voice repo are modified. On top of the standard tau-voice agent system prompt, we prepend an additional scaffold system message that defines each agent's identity and role (the real-time voice agent vs. the background tool-calling agent), the responsibilities each one owns, and how the two coordinate and share context.
Full base splits evaluated on all three domains (retail 114, airline 50, telecom 114), 1 trial per task, --speech-complexity regular. User simulator is the standard v1.0 pipeline (gpt-4.1). User-side voices are local ElevenLabs personas created via the standard setup_voices script; not Sierra-managed submission voices.
Compared with our earlier Pine Voice Preview, this release includes many model updates and engineering improvements, including the background agent now running gemini-4-argon at reasoning_effort=high.
